name: v1_default
_comment_models: 42 models total: the 30 TabArena-native models onboarded/wired this session (16 previously-listed-but-unwired, fixed in 5c57fe4, plus 14 newly onboarded in 3 batches: 98c44ad/90f49a8/a6a6986) plus 11 pre-existing RamanBench-native custom architectures verified against the v1 pipeline in a separate follow-up (aae8393: ARSENAL, COATNET, DEEPCNN, FCRESNEXT, RAMANFORMER, RAMANNET, RAMANTRANSFORMER, REZERONET, ROCKET, SANET, plus TABPFN-WIDE re-added after aae8393 fixed a real CPU-fallback bug -- device was hardcoded 'cpu' despite info.py tagging compute='gpu', so it silently never used the GPU it was allocated). All 42 confirmed to resolve cleanly via raman_bench.models.registry.infer_model_cls. PLS is listed LAST, not first: pick_chunk() picks the FIRST model in this list with a nonempty backlog and takes a full chunk_size from it before ever looking at the next model (strict priority, not round-robin) -- PLS already has a large in-progress backlog from its long head start, so putting it first would starve every other model of new submissions until PLS's backlog was fully drained. PLS's own already-queued/running SLURM tasks are unaffected by this ordering (only NEW chunk submissions go through pick_chunk). The 11 custom architectures have no existing production backlog, so their relative order doesn't matter much; placed after the 30 TabArena models (which were dry-run-verified first) and still ahead of PLS. Deliberately still excludes AUTOGLUON only (whole-predictor meta-preset, not a per-model ConfigGenerator -- can't be wired into run_experiment.py's one-model-per-job design as-is; GBM was never part of either onboarding effort and stays out until its own verification pass). WATCH ITEM: TABPFN-WIDE's GPU fix (aae8393) was verified functionally correct but the actual speedup was NOT confirmed on real hardware (the dev machine fixing it had no CUDA) -- watch its first real runs, especially against the 3 large classification datasets it's eligible for (mlrod 130,061 rows, bacteria_identification 78,500 rows, wheat_lines 53,134 rows); mlrod already gets the blanket 10800s dataset-level override below, but if CUDA doesn't actually get exercised in the real SLURM allocation for any reason, a naive linear extrapolation from aae8393's own CPU-only scaling probe (20 rows->5.7s, 350 rows->88.2s) suggests even that 10800s budget could plausibly be too small at mlrod's full scale -- no override added preemptively since this is speculative extrapolation over a ~370x range, not calibration evidence; add one if a real run confirms it's needed, same convention as EBM/ORIONMSP below. 43rd model, RAMANPFN, added after merging feat/prep-effects-methods (frozen-TabPFN dual-view GCU+LVSE architecture, Pan et al. arXiv:2608.02157) -- GPU (compute='gpu', same tier as MITRA/TABDPT/etc.), no existing backlog, placed among the other custom architectures ahead of PLS for the same reason. Verified end-to-end via a real local run_experiment.py smoke test (alzheimer, config_index 0): 0.9998 validation ROC AUC, metric_error~0.001, real results.pkl produced -- not just the unit-level model tests from its own onboarding commit. TABPFN-WIDE REMOVED 2026-09-18 (down to 42 models): tabpfnwide exact-pins an old tabpfn, permanently incompatible with tabpfn>=9.0.0 (required for the newly-onboarded TabPFN-3.5) -- see pyproject.toml models extra comment. Existing TABPFN-WIDE results stay as historical data. TABPFN-V3.5 (the model this comment's floor bump was actually made for) added 2026-09-24 as its own onboarding commit -- placed next to TABPFN-V3, confirmed to resolve cleanly via raman_bench.models.registry.infer_model_cls, no existing backlog. RAMANTRANSFORMER briefly removed and same-day restored 2026-09-26 (still 43 models): initially excluded as the worst-performing custom architecture in the v0.1 leaderboard, sharing the same NaN-validation-loss collapse class documented for RAMANFORMER/SANET (GitHub issue #10) -- confirmed live on the v1 cluster once its GPU-tier resource-declaration bug was fixed (2026-09-25: 47/312 tasks failed for RAMANFORMER alone with the identical error; RAMANTRANSFORMER showed the same pattern), and its two running k8s jobs (rb-ramantransformer-full/large) were cancelled. On reconsideration, this was inconsistent with the standing 'benchmark what they did, document failures rather than exclude' policy already applied to RAMANFORMER (kept running despite the same failure class, letting the leaderboard's imputed-% transparency show the real result) -- restored to keep both models on equal footing. Listed LAST in this array (after PLS) and, separately, placed at the END of the manual k8s resubmission queue this session is tracking, so it is deliberately the last model resubmitted, not run immediately.
_comment_compute_scaling: num_bag_folds (was 8) and time_limit (was 3600) both cut 2026-09-25 as a deliberate compute-scaling decision, alongside target_list.json's n_repeats=1 (see configs/v1/README.md). Impact differs by model class: compute-bound models (LIMIX/TABICL/TABFM/TabPFN-family -- finish well under their old time budget regardless of fold count) get a roughly proportional ~(3/8) compute cut per task with no real quality risk. Time-budget-bound models (MITRA is the confirmed case: consistently used ~59 of its 60 allotted minutes every fold, never early-stopping) are a real risk here -- AutoGluon's fold time-budgeting (time_limit_fold = (time_left/folds_left)*0.8) means the full 600s is now split across only 3 folds instead of 8, so MITRA-class fine-tuning gets meaningfully fewer training epochs per fold than before, likely undertrained relative to its earlier (still not fully converged) runs. Not fixed here -- flagged so a future review of MITRA/RAMANFORMER/REALMLP/TABM-class results interprets a score drop correctly (compute starvation, not necessarily a worse architecture). model_time_limit_overrides below are unaffected (they're already-calibrated absolute floors well above 600s for specific slow/wide (model, dataset) pairs) and stay in force.
_comment_max_train_samples_overrides: Global (every model, both SLURM and k8s backends -- see cluster/submit_job.py's resolve_max_train_samples), unlike model_time_limit_overrides which is model-specific. Added 2026-09-25 after REZERONET's real TimeLimitExceeded on mlrod (130,061 rows) under the 600s/3-bag-fold compute-scaling settings: 90/93 large-pod tasks succeeded with real, confirmed GPU utilization (the GPU-tier resource-declaration fix, see bridge_bases._GPURequiredBridge), only mlrod's 3 tasks (repeat=0, folds 0-2) failed on time budget. 10000 is a deliberate row cap (~13x fewer rows than mlrod's 130061) chosen to fit comfortably in the 600s/3-fold budget while keeping a substantial training set -- not recalibrated against a real measured runtime the way time_limit_overrides' 10800 was, so revisit if a model still times out on mlrod at this cap.
_comment_large_datasets: k8s-only (submit_full_benchmark.py's k8s branch): routed to a separate single pod on a bigger GPU (H100/H200) instead of the main A100 pod, so the main sweep isn't dominated by these outliers. Two disjoint kinds of 'large', both real: the top 6 by row count (mlrod 130061, bacteria_identification 78500, wheat_lines 53134, serum_prostate_cancer 12601, sugar_mixtures_low_snr 7840, bioprocess_substrates 6960 -- clear cliff after these, next is 12601 already listed then a drop to 4020) stress GPU batch-size/training memory; the 9 extremely wide ones (~11084-11689 features, 14-235 rows: acetic_acid_species, citric_acid_species, flow_microgel_synthesis, formic_acid_species, itaconic_acid_species, levulinic_acid_species, microgel_size_raw_global, microgel_synthesis, succinic_acid_species) stress feature-dimension memory instead (PCA/GCU representation size, TabPFN's per-forward-pass feature cap) -- unrelated mechanism, just also 'large' in a different axis. 6 more equally-wide microgel_size_*_global variants exist in data/precomputed/dataset_stats.json but aren't in target_list.json (not part of the routine sweep), so they're excluded here too.
_comment_model_time_limit_overrides: EBM's real TimeLimitExceeded on wide datasets was mostly interpret's own O(n_features^2) interaction-ranking pre-scan (see Prep_EBM._fit's docstring) -- fixed at the model level (interactions=0 above 4000 features), not by budget alone. A real calibration run post-fix (microgel_synthesis, 11084 features, run_experiment.py --model EBM --time-limit 900 --num-bag-folds 8; this measurement predates the 2026-09-25 removal of small-dataset bag-fold auto-scaling, so it ran at 2 effective folds for this 14-row dataset -- num_bag_folds no longer scales down for any dataset size now, so a rerun would use the routine 3-fold (or whatever --num-bag-folds is passed) instead) finished in 426s wall time (400s training) at 2 folds, already well inside the 3600s default. These 5400s entries are headroom, not a required fix: the other 9 targets in the same 11084-11689-feature cluster have more rows and so used the full 8 bag folds at calibration time (now always whatever --num-bag-folds is configured, currently 3), extrapolating to roughly 4x -> ~1700s -- 5400s leaves ample margin over that for a slower cluster CPU than the one calibrated on, and only more so now that folds never scale below the configured value. ORIONMSP's pharmaceutical_ingredients entry is similarly a safety margin, not the primary fix -- see cluster/profiles/htw.yaml's ORIONMSP mem_tier: a real local run there (2 bag folds) finished fitting in ~175s but then crashed from memory (~25-27GB RSS on a 36GB machine), i.e. this dataset's real confirmed risk is memory, not time. LR's entry is a bare number (not a dataset-keyed dict) -- a blanket override applied regardless of dataset (see cluster/submit_job.py::resolve_time_limit's scalar-override handling). Confirmed real: LR's bagged fold fit on wheat_lines/bacteria_identification takes ~530-560s/fold x 8 sequential folds (~4240-4480s), past the 3600s default, so AutoGluon's fold-fitting strategy extrapolated from an early fold and aborted with TimeLimitExceeded before the (finite, just slower-than-guessed) remaining folds got a chance -- same failure mode already seen for PLS on mlrod, just not yet hit for LR until these two datasets. Under the routine config_index=0 backlog (no HPO search opted in), a time cap on a model like LR doesn't bound anything meaningful -- it only risks this same early-abort happening again on some other not-yet-encountered (model, dataset) pair. 800000s (~9.3 days) is comfortably under the real backstop, the SLURM array's own --time (the profile's default_time, 10 days) -- independent of this value.
